To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a novel chemically stabilized form E7SOx, based on a recombinant HPV E7‐based vaccine, is highly effective in preventing and treating E7‐expressed HPV tumor models.

we have developed a novel HPV E7‐based vaccine candidate, with high stability and immunogenicity, which is able to protect mice against tumor development and significantly delay tumor growth when administered as a therapeutic vaccine.

we have developed a novel chemically stabilized E7 vaccine, based on the self‐assembling E7SOs, that induces a long‐lasting protection in a murine cervical cancer model and that can be used as a therapeutic vaccine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel HPV vaccine candidate that could be used for prophylactic and therapeutic purposes, and which is highly stable and inexpensive.
the design, development and characterization of a highly stable and safe vaccine for cervical and other HPV‐induced cancers, which could be used as a prophylactic vaccine in the future.
developing a new generation of highly stable and effective vaccines against cervical cancer, with a potential application for the development of other cancer vaccines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
E7SOs are a promising HPV‐based vaccine candidate for cervical cancer and other HPV‐induced tumors.
our E7SO vaccine candidate is an attractive candidate for clinical trials, given its high immunogenicity, stability, safety, and low‐cost.

E7SOs, in combination with ODN adjuvant, are highly immunogenic, long‐lasting, stable and safe, and therefore, constitute a promising HPV vaccine candidate for the treatment of mucosal HPV‐induced tumors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the E7SO vaccine candidate is an effective, safe and low‐cost immunotherapeutic approach to prevent and/or treat HPV‐associated tumors.
E7SOs, and especially the E7SO _{x}, represent an innovative and cost‐effective vaccine strategy for the treatment of cervical and other HPV‐associated cancers.
E7SOs are highly resistant to proteases, chemical, and thermal degradation, and are able to induce a potent immune response in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of E7SOs as a vaccine against HPV‐related diseases is a viable strategy to prevent or treat HPV infection.

the E7SO vaccine candidate has a great potential to be used in the treatment of HPV‐related cancers, and it is a promising candidate for the development of an affordable vaccine against cervical cancer.
the E7SO vaccine candidate is a promising therapeutic vaccine for the treatment of cervical and other anogenital cancers.
